speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the blisters on your forearm and the ulcers on your mucosal surfaces in detail, including when they started and any associated symptoms like fever or pain.

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Oral and Genital Aphthous Ulcers secondary to Captopril-induced Angioedema. (Note: The "blisters" described as painful when eating/intercourse likely represent early angioedema or severe aphthous ulcers, a known side effect of ACE inhibitors like captopril, rather than a primary skin condition like Stevens-Johnson Syndrome given the lack of widespread skin involvement and specific drug history).
